canonical_name: TÜBİTAK 2202 — Ulusal Bilim Olimpiyatları (National Science Olympiads)
organization: TÜBİTAK — Bilim İnsanı Destek Programları Başkanlığı (BİDEB), Yarışmalar Grubu
strategic_role: THIS IS THE ENTRY ROUTE. For a student in Türkiye, IMO / IPhO / IChO / IBO / IOI are NOT directly applicable — the only way in is by climbing this national ladder. Recording the international olympiads without this record would give Turkish students a destination with no road to it.
grade_eligibility: Grades 8-11 for most branches; grades 9-11 for Coğrafya, Matematik and Bilgisayar; grades 5-8 for the two ortaokul (middle-school) branches. Final-year high school students are excluded across the board.
grade_note: DECISION-CRITICAL TIMING: son sınıf (final-year) students are excluded. A student who waits until 12th grade has permanently missed this route — and with it the route to every international science olympiad. This makes it an early-planning item for 14-16 year olds, exactly ORYN's core age band.
eligibility_note: Studying in Türkiye or KKTC. Same study-location (not citizenship) basis as 2204-A.

application_url_note: There is NO direct application URL and there must never be one in this record. §2.1: 'Participation in an IMO is by invitation only.' A student applies to their NATIONAL olympiad, not to the IMO.
entry_mechanism_verbatim: §2.1 'Participation in an IMO is by invitation only. Each invited country (or territory in some exceptional cases approved by the IMO Board) is entitled to send a team consisting of up to six contestants (the "Contestants"), a Leader (also: Jury member), and a Deputy Leader.' §2.2 'A Country's Contestants should be selected through that Country's national Mathematical Olympiad or equivalent selection programme.'
deadline_note: No student-facing deadline exists at the IMO level by construction. The actionable deadline is the student's own national olympiad's — for Türkiye that is TÜBİTAK 2202 (CR1-030).
age_rule_verbatim: §2.2 'Contestants must have been born on or after 1 July in the year x−20 where x is the year of participation at the IMO.'
age_rule_computed: For IMO 2027 this means born on or after 1 July 2007.
age_rule_note: Do NOT flatten to maximum_age=19: the rule is a birth-date cutoff relative to the competition year, which is not the same as an age on the day.
enrolment_rule_verbatim: §2.2 'Contestants must have been normally enrolled in full-time primary or secondary education on or after 1 December in the year prior to the IMO, or, in the case of home-schooled students, must not have received a high-school diploma (or equivalent), and must be working toward such a credential on 1 December.'
enrolment_note: Home-schooled students are explicitly accommodated — worth surfacing, it is unusual and easy to assume otherwise.
citizenship_rule_verbatim: §2.2 'Contestants of Country X should normally be citizens of Country X, but genuine long-term foreign residents who are not citizens (and who are being educated in Country X) are permitted to be in the IMO team of Country X provided that the student has already spent at least one full academic year being educated in Country X, and will spend a total of at least two years in full-time education in Country X before they leave secondary education. Such a foreign education must be for a bona fide family reason, and not artificially to change national IMO status.'
citizenship_note: DIRECTLY ANSWERS ORYN's international-student case. A student at an international school abroad can represent their country of residence, but only on a documented two-year education test, and only for genuine family reasons. This is precisely the question an expat or third-culture student would ask and it is answerable from the primary source.
anti_shopping_rule_verbatim: §2.2 'Note that IMO tourism is not permitted: a student may not attempt the final selection examinations of more than one country in a given IMO year.'
eligible_countries: VIA_NATIONAL_OLYMPIAD_ONLY — invited countries only; no open worldwide entry
cost_note: NOT STATED in the General Regulations for contestants. Costs are settled between organisers and participating countries, not charged to students directly; do not record 0.00 without a statement.
fetch_method: WebFetch + local pypdf extraction (WebFetch could not parse the regulations PDF)
why_high_value: The most prestigious secondary-school competition in the world, entirely absent from the corpus. Its correct student-facing action is 'enter your national olympiad', which is a different and much earlier action than 'apply to the IMO' — the exact error a naive record would cause.
unresolved: Regulations version retrieved is 'approved at the IMO 2025'; check for a newer version before the 2027 cycle.

organization: IOI (International Olympiad in Informatics) / IOI Foundation
entry_mechanism_verbatim: S2.3 'Each participating Country is represented by a National Delegation... includes a team of one to four Contestants and, if there is more than one Contestant, may include a Deputy Leader.' N2.5.1 'It is firmly recommended that Contestants should have participated in a local, regional or national informatics competition in their Country as a pre-selection for the IOI, and that they belong to the winners of that competition.'
entry_mechanism_note: Note the precise wording: national pre-selection is 'firmly recommended', NOT stated as mandatory — weaker than IMO's 'should be selected through that Country's national Mathematical Olympiad'. In practice the country's delegation decides. Do not tell a student the national route is optional.
team_size_exception_verbatim: E2.3.1 'If the Host Country for IOI'n wants to invite delegations with more or less than four Contestants, it must be approved at a GA meeting during IOI'n-1.'
age_rule_verbatim: S2.5(2) 'is not older than twenty years on the 1st of July of the year of IOI'n.' N2.5.2 'Every contestant at IOI'n (held in year n) must have been born on or after 1st July, in the year n − 20.'
enrolment_rule_verbatim: S2.5(1) 'for the majority of the period 1 September to 31 December in the year before IOI'n: - was enrolled in a school at a level of secondary education or lower, in the Country they are representing; and - was not enrolled in a degree programme at a tertiary education institution with a half-time or greater load.'
studying_abroad_rule_verbatim: S2.5 'Exceptions to this may be requested through the IC. Students who are studying abroad may instead represent the Country of their nationality.'
studying_abroad_note: IMPORTANT CONTRAST WITH IMO. IOI gives students studying abroad an explicit fallback: represent your country of NATIONALITY. IMO instead lets long-term foreign residents represent their country of RESIDENCE subject to a two-year education test. The two olympiads resolve the same expat situation in opposite directions — an ORYN advisor must not generalise one rule to the other.

organization: Stockholm Water Foundation (founded 1997 by the Stockholm International Water Institute, SIWI)
secondary_character: genuine research — projects must use scientifically accepted methods
not_to_be_confused_with: The professional Stockholm Water Prize, a career-achievement award for established researchers and institutions. The live corpus row titled 'Stockholm Water Prize' (official_url stockholmwaterfoundation.org/big_project_page/nominate/) is that professional award and is NOT a student opportunity — separately confirmed by oryn-ce via kva.se. This record is the youth prize and is a DIFFERENT ENTITY, not a correction of that row.
entry_mechanism_verbatim: 'Only projects nominated by their national organizer in each participating country are eligible to compete internationally.'; 'your first step is to connect with your national organizer (check the map), who will guide you through the process in your country.'
age_rule_verbatim: 'The Stockholm Junior Water Prize is for young minds aged 15 to 20 years old who are currently attending secondary high school or its equivalent. Note that you cannot submit a project if enrolled at a university.'
team_rule_verbatim: 'Whether you're working alone or with a team, we welcome your brilliance, though a maximum of two students can represent the project in Stockholm.'
team_rule_note: Team size for the PROJECT is unrestricted; only representation at the Stockholm final is capped at two. Worth stating precisely — a five-person school team can enter, but must choose two to travel.
research_requirement_verbatim: 'All projects must be research-oriented, using scientifically accepted methods for investigation, experimentation, monitoring, and reporting results.'
research_requirement_note: This is what makes SJWP a genuine research opportunity rather than an ideas competition — and it is why it belongs in the same conversation as ISEF and BL4S.
scope_verbatim: 'water quality, water resources management, water protection, water and wastewater treatment, as well as water education and the social aspects of water'
scope_note: Explicitly includes SOCIAL SCIENCES and education, not only lab science. A student interested in economics or policy can enter with a water-policy project — unusually broad for a science prize.
turkey_national_organizer: General Directorate of State Hydraulic Works (Devlet Su İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü, DSİ) — İsmet İnönü Blv., Çankaya/Ankara, Turkey

turkey_organizer_identity_caution: A naive text search for 'turk' on that dataset returns TWO hits: 'Youth Engineers Alliance, Ashgabat, TURKMENISTAN' and the Ankara entry. The Turkmenistan row is a substring false positive. Türkiye's organiser is the Ankara one.
eligible_countries_note: 39 identifiable countries from 40 organizer records; one record ('National Youth Science Consortium (NYSC)') carries no resolvable country. This list is the definitive eligibility set — SJWP is NOT open worldwide, it is open where a national organizer exists.
deadline_note: No international deadline exists; each national organizer sets its own timeline. For Türkiye the actionable date is DSİ's, which is not published on the SWF site.

Absent from the corpus, while the similarly-named professional award sits in it wrongly.

secondary_character: genuine research — the oldest and most prestigious US pre-college science research competition
self_registration_note: Unlike the flagship olympiads and unlike ISEF, a student applies DIRECTLY. No national body, no affiliated fair, no institutional registration. Rare and worth surfacing.
deadline_note: 74 days out from retrieval — one of the few genuinely actionable near-term deadlines found in this whole lane.
eligibility_verbatim_us: 'Any student who is living in and attending their last year of secondary school in the US and its territories may apply, regardless of citizenship.'
eligibility_verbatim_citizens_abroad: 'Students who are US citizens living abroad may also qualify.'
eligibility_verbatim_exclusion: 'Students attending American schools abroad, but who are not US citizens, are not eligible.'
eligibility_note: THE RULE IS RESIDENCE-AND-SCHOOL BASED, NOT CITIZENSHIP BASED — and the third clause is the trap. A Turkish student at an American school in Istanbul is NOT eligible. A Turkish student who has moved to the US and is in their final year IS eligible, citizenship irrelevant. Any record that flattens this to 'United States' in eligible_countries will mislead both groups in opposite directions.
grade_rule: Last year of secondary school (final-year students only)
team_rule_verbatim: 'No; only independent, individual research is eligible.'
research_window_verbatim: 'Entrants may submit research projects performed in any year of school, over any length of time.'
contrast_with_isef: SAME ORGANISER, OPPOSITE RULES — high-value advisory fact. ISEF: teams of up to three, research capped at 'no more than 12 months of continuous research', entry only via an affiliated fair, grades 9-12. STS: individuals ONLY, research from ANY year over ANY length, direct application, final-year students only. A student choosing between them is choosing between two genuinely different formats, and the same multi-year project that STS welcomes would breach ISEF's 12-month rule.
selectivity: 'around 2,600 students enter'; top 300 named Scholars; top 40 named Finalists.
prizes_verbatim: '$3.1 million in awards are distributed annually, including the first place prize of $250,000'

canonical_name: International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics (IOAA)
organization: IOAA (President: Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education, Mumbai)
age_rule_verbatim: 'Must have been born on or after 1 July 2006.'
age_rule_note: For IOAA 2026 — the same year-relative birth-date construction as IMO and IOI (effectively under 20), not a plain maximum_age. Recomputed each edition.
education_rule_verbatim: 'Must not have completed high school (Grade 12 or equivalent) before 1 January 2026.'
CITIZENSHIP_RULE_verbatim: 'Must be either a citizen or a regular resident of the country they represent in IOAA 2026.'
THE_THIRD_ANSWER_TO_THE_SAME_QUESTION: This is the THIRD distinct way the flagship olympiads resolve the expatriate student's case, and it is the most permissive of the three. IMO: long-term foreign residents may represent their country of residence, but only after one full academic year there and a commitment to two years total, 'for a bona fide family reason'. IOI: students studying abroad 'may instead represent the Country of their nationality' — a nationality fallback. IOAA: **citizen OR regular resident**, plain disjunction, no duration test, no stated purpose test. A Turkish student at an international school abroad has three different answers depending on which olympiad they ask.
why_that_matters_for_the_product: It is direct evidence that eligibility cannot be generalised across even structurally identical competitions. These three bodies run the same kind of event, for the same age group, selected the same way — and answer the single most common question an international student has in three incompatible ways. Any advisor heuristic learned from one will be wrong for the others.
team_leader_rule_verbatim: 'Must be professional astronomers, amateur astronomers, university or school teachers, or past winners of national or international Olympiads... Must be proficient in reading, writing, and conversing in English.'
team_leader_note: Unusually broad — an AMATEUR astronomer or a past olympiad winner can lead a delegation. Relevant to a country without an established programme.
newcomer_note_verbatim: 'New countries may consider participating without any students'
newcomer_note: An explicit on-ramp for countries with no national olympiad yet — leaders may attend to observe before sending students. Rare and worth recording; it means 'my country doesn't participate' is not necessarily permanent.
deadline_note: No student-facing deadline; entry is via national selection, as with the rest of the flagship tier.
fetch_method: Browser pane (ioaastrophysics.org returns 403 to WebFetch); eligibility text sits inside a collapsed accordion and had to be read from the DOM rather than the rendered page
